decision: Space name, project and goal render as the `space` prompt section; thread.create is an owner/Puck op and a `thread_create` tool; xin.puck lists Puck conversations and scopeOf treats any listed conversation as Puck
why: the split left the goal dead and left the owner and Puck unable to start a thread without a space coordinator; Puck needed somewhere to keep several conversations
evidence: plugins/workspace/index.ts section("space"); plugins/orchestrator/threads.ts thread.create; src/contracts/puck.ts; gate fmt, lint, types, test and bundle green
result: accepted; the root stays the default Puck conversation and is not stored in xin.puck

decision: thread.archive sets an optional flag on xin.thread and the home projection and thread_list hide it; artifacts are one xin.artifacts doc per thread with a revision and a 10-artifact/1 MB bound, exposed as artifact.* ops and a tool-* row
why: an archived thread must stay readable and its conversation must survive; a per-thread artifact map keeps reads and writes atomic with the transcript and avoids a new doc-family mechanism
evidence: plugins/orchestrator/threads.ts thread.archive; plugins/artifacts/*; plugins/workspace/workspace.ts projection skip; gate fmt, lint, types, test and bundle green
result: accepted; no comments and no old-revision history until a use case needs them

decision: Add web_search (DuckDuckGo HTML) and web_fetch (public http(s) to text) as one built-in row, both through jobs.tool
why: no key or configuration is available for a search API, the two tools cover lookup and reading, and the job wrapper gives the run a timeout/report path; the spec scope changes from files-only to files plus the public web
evidence: plugins/web/web.test.ts (5 tests); gate fmt/lint/types/test/bundle green (440 passed, 15 skipped)

decision: The market's default index is the build's catalog, not a hosted URL
why: owner wants a fresh install to browse with no setup. A hosted default would add an external dependency, a fetch on first open with no network, and a file to keep in sync; the build already knows its packages
evidence: builtinIndex in plugins/market/index.ts groups plugin.catalog by package; load() prepends it and leaves market.refresh summaries to configured indexes; market.entry reads a provided package's rows from the composition; market.test.ts searches with no index and asserts zero requests, then shows the preset rows
result: kept; no new public word, no config, no fetch

decision: The shipped full and minimal presets moved from tools to plugins
why: they are rows in xin-plugin-presets/package.json and the slice-2 rename made tools invalid; a failed preset row would silently disappear from preset.list while every conversation fell back to all extensions
evidence: package.json now declares plugins "all" and ["tool-memory","tool-skills"]; presets.test.ts adds "ships the full and minimal presets active", which fails if either row stops validating
result: kept; descriptions now say plugin, not tool row

decision: Prompts and skills are row contributions filtered by the same preset rule as extensions
why: most author value is a prompt or a skill, and neither was a contribution before; both are not extensions, so they need their own source and one shared visibility rule. The source is the row id, exactly as ctx.pi.installed records it
evidence: contracts/prompts.ts adds PromptEntry with source; plugins/presets/prompts.ts merges stored and contributed prompts and filters by presetAllows; tool-skills filters the section and the skill tool with ctx.kernel.pluginOfRow(row); test/plugins/contrib.ts contributes one of each; presets.test.ts keeps both with a preset that names contrib and drops both without it
result: kept; prompt.list filters only when given a conversation, and skill.list (owner read) still lists every skill; the skill tool and section are scoped

decision: Xin drops the six pi indexes that no query reads
why: each index adds a row to every write of its table; pi 1.5 scans tasks only by status and kind, submissions only by status, documents only by scope, and conversations only by owner task, so tasks-by-conversation, tasks-by-abort, tasks-by-background, submissions-by-conversation, documents-by-scope-kind and conversations-by-owner-conversation are write-only
evidence: test/load.bench.ts: 182 to 131 rows written per message at 100 threads, reads unchanged at 229; grep of every scanTasks/scanSubmissions/scanDocuments/scanConversations call in pi 1.5 shows no query on those columns
result: kept; the list is in src/kernel/pi.ts with the reason, and document-revisions-by-kind stays because the base lookup reads it; superseded 2026-11-10: pi's tables and their indexes no longer exist. The harness runs on MemoryStorage and reaches disk as a journal (rows 281, 307-309), so src/kernel/pi.ts keeps no index list

decision: The intake and receipt indexes go, and their tables are scanned instead
why: inbound-target and receipts-at each cost a row on every write to save a scan of a handful of pending rows or a day of receipts; writes cost a thousand times a read
evidence: migration 10 drops both; about 4 rows a message in the 100-thread load, and a cold message reads 1,821 rows instead of 1,516
result: kept; the trade is about 300 reads per cold message for 4 writes per message; superseded 2026-11-10: migration 11 recreated receipts_at, inbound_target and inbound_batch once the journal cut the write bill, and migration 12 dropped the inbound table with its indexes; the queue is the xin.intake document (row 313)

decision: Expose MCP resources and prompts as read-only deferred tools under tool-mcp, gated by the server capabilities
why: resources and prompts are data, not side effects; keeping them on the same extension means one preset or row switch hides tools, resources and prompts together, and threads inherit it; sampling, elicitation and the GET stream stay out
evidence: plugins/mcp/mcp.test.ts (resources/prompts test); gate fmt/lint/types/test/bundle green (441 passed, 15 skipped)

decision: Read-only git history uses one GitHub repository named in project.settings.git and four tools: git_log, git_show, git_diff, git_blame
why: no checkout or code execution exists in the Worker, so a remote read-only API is the only real git source; project settings keep the repo out of tool arguments, and GitHub is the first provider because its REST and GraphQL cover all four reads
evidence: plugins/git/git.test.ts (3 tests); gate fmt/lint/types/test/bundle green (444 passed, 15 skipped)
result: accepted; GitLab and local checkouts are not included

decision: pi's state runs on MemoryStorage and reaches disk as a journal of its commits
why: a message wrote 131 billed rows because every task phase, document and index was its own row; kiko measured the same shape and wins on writes, not reads, so the win is the write shape
evidence: src/kernel/journal.ts; 100-thread load: 131 to 26 rows written and 229 to 39 read per message, 523 to 62 statements
result: kept; one row per settled turn, plus configuration and a 1 MB bound

decision: The journal checkpoints every 256 rows and truncates the prefix
why: without it a cold start replays every row ever written, which is the cost kiko accepts and the owner asked not to
evidence: cold message after eviction reads about 310 rows, ~280 of them replaying a near-full journal and 1-3 the checkpoint parts; the journal costs about 5.8 rows a message, including the checkpoint rewrite and truncation

decision: Writes are durable at a flush, not at every commit
why: a journal row per commit would be the row count we just removed; the flush points are the settled turn, configuration documents, and 1 MB
evidence: an eviction mid-turn re-runs that turn, tools included, and the client's request id keeps it from running twice; every eviction test and the reporter path pass
result: kept; recorded in 11-failures-and-cost.md, and the trade the owner accepted

decision: A thread touches only its own thread, and the recovery horizon folds into the alarm minimum
why: canUseThread let a thread read and write a sibling's artifacts, cancel a sibling's job and read a sibling's status; the recovery alarm only ran when nothing was due, and the weekly file sweep always supplied one
evidence: artifacts/jobs/clock tests: sibling artifact ops rejected, sibling job cancel false, active wake with a weekly due gets an alarm within 2 minutes; full gate and benchmark green
result: accepted; plugin.list test covers the disabled rows

decision: The checkpoint rewrite is one transaction, replay reads only seq > checkpoint, and truncation deletes only seq <= checkpoint
why: removing the old checkpoint and the journal in separate statements left a crash window with neither; deleting every journal row made correctness rest on an invariant instead of the sequence
evidence: journal tests: covered row skipped, failed checkpoint write leaves the old checkpoint, a newer journal row survives truncation
result: accepted; cold boot reads asserted > 0 in test/load.bench.ts

decision: Web and git ship as disabled rows in the profile, not as absent bundles
why: removing the bundles made the rows unreachable: plugin.list could not show them and plugin.enable could not mount them without a rebuild
evidence: plugins/web and plugins/git package.json bundle rows carry disabled: true; plugin.list test shows tool-web disabled then enabled; 15-web and 16-git say off by default
result: accepted; tests enable the row explicitly

decision: The intake queue is the session document xin.intake, not a host table
why: the queue was 14 of the 26 rows a message wrote (INSERT inbound plus three index rows, and three UPDATEs across those indexes); a document commit is one journal row, and its delta ops are small
evidence: plugins/intake/gateway.ts, src/contracts/intake.ts; 100-thread load: 26 to 16 written and 42 to 21 read per message
result: src/db.ts migration 12 drops inbound; src/kernel/dbtables.ts no longer names it

decision: One items array holds pending, claimed and done, with status and nextId for SQLite's rowid
why: batchId alone cannot tell claimed from done, and intake.batch feeds message.retry after a failed turn, possibly days later; deleting an item at finish would break the retry
evidence: plugins/intake/gateway.ts start() prunes done items older than 7 days; plugins/failures/failures.test.ts retry still resubmits the stored body
result: done items stay 7 days, pruned at boot only

decision: message.send opts out of receipts (receipts: false); its intake item answers a resend
why: the batch submission's request id is batch:<batchId> and is shared by several commands, so it cannot answer a per-command resend; the item's commandId can, in any state, for 7 days (longer than the 24 h receipt it replaces)
evidence: src/ops.ts Op.receipts; plugins/intake/gateway.test.ts "stores a retried message command once" still asserts one item and one turn; the thread.send replay test still deletes a receipt to force a duplicate
result: every other op keeps the receipts table and its behaviour

decision: dispatch claims inside a commit before the intake/batch waterfall runs
why: the documented "a claimed batch is about to be dispatched" has to hold before a side-effecting listener sees it; running the waterfall first would save a row but move goals.admit and the withdraws into the pending window
evidence: plugins/intake/gateway.ts dispatch(); plugins/intake/batch.test.ts and the goals rounds tests pass
result: persist is a second commit, free when no listener rewrote a body (an empty commit stores nothing)

decision: markDone at submission settle is its own commit, not folded into a later enqueue
why: folding it would leave items claimed in the meantime, so a claim at boot would look like work to replay
evidence: plugins/intake/gateway.test.ts resubmits a claimed batch after eviction; done items are visible once the turn settles

decision: Migration 12 drops inbound, so a message still in the 2 s debounce at the upgrade is lost
why: at personal scale, behind a laneless debounce, an upgrade mid-debounce is rare and the client can resend
evidence: src/db.ts migration 12

decision: The measured result is 16 written and 21 read per message, not the estimated 12 to 13
why: each of the three added commits is stored as one journal row and truncated in turn (about 2.6 rows with the plumbing's truncation), so the queue's 14 rows and the receipt's 3 give back only 17
evidence: XIN_LOAD=1 load bench: turnPerMessage 49 calls, 21 reads, 16 writes; turnSql 12402c/6122r/4089w over 300 messages; journal 6.67 inserts and 6.83 deletes a message
result: bounds lowered to 65 calls, 32 reads, 22 writes; src/cost.test.ts bounds 18/22 and 36/46

decision: A commit waits for a checkpoint in flight, and a journal row whose commits the checkpoint covers is skipped on replay
why: the checkpoint captured its sequence before awaiting the snapshot, so a commit applied during the snapshot could be baked into the checkpoint while its journal row survived; replaying it threw and JournalStorage.open killed every op on the home, and a checkpoint error that escaped commit() left #journalled over the threshold so every later commit retried it
evidence: src/kernel/journal.ts commit()/checkpoint()/#restore; src/kernel/journal.test.ts "keeps a commit that lands during a checkpoint out of its snapshot" and "replays only the commits a later journal row adds to a covered checkpoint" fail at a61b166 with "Commit sequence 7 does not strictly increase" / "ID 402 already belongs to document" and pass after
result: kept; a checkpoint that throws still escapes commit() once, but the count restarts before the attempt so it is not retried by every later commit

decision: POST /v1/repair on Home answers without the kernel: it reports the boot failure, and drops the journal rows or the checkpoint too before opening again
why: a home whose journal or checkpoint cannot be read 503s on every route, including the ops that could repair it, so a deploy could not fix it; no route or op could reach storage when boot fails
evidence: src/host.ts #open/#repair; src/host.test.ts "answers a repair route when its journal cannot be read, and opens again once the journal is dropped" and "refuses to drop the journal of a home that is open" fail at a61b166 (503 for the repair route) and pass after
result: kept; drop:journal loses the state since the last checkpoint and drop:all loses everything, so the route reports both counts and refuses an open home

decision: The files hook scopes pi's read tool like write and edit, after normalising the path the way pi resolves it
why: only write and edit were checked, so any thread could read /me and other projects, and pi strips a leading @ before resolving while the hook did not, so @/me/x.txt was checked as /@/me/x.txt and written to /me/x.txt
evidence: plugins/files/files.ts scoped()/toolPath(); plugins/files/files.test.ts "blocks a thread's pi read of /me and of another project" and "blocks a write to /me written with a leading @" fail at a61b166 and pass after
result: kept; WriteScope is renamed FileScope and the block messages say "use" rather than "write" because reads share the rule

decision: git_show and git_diff refuse a ref with an empty, dot, dot-dot, backslash or percent segment
why: the ref is encoded into the URL path and .. survived it, so ../../ reached another repository with the home's GitHub token
evidence: plugins/git/git.ts refPath(); plugins/git/git.test.ts "refuses a ref that would walk out of the project repository" fails at a61b166 with a request whose URL contains .. and passes after
result: kept; git_log and git_blame pass the ref as a query value and a GraphQL expression, so they need no path check

decision: The clock isolates each timer, and arm() rejects when the alarm write fails; alarm() arms in a finally
why: one throwing timer skipped the rest and escaped alarm() before the closing arm, and a failing due() aborted the DO as "alarm write failed" while every caller was resolved as if the alarm had been written
evidence: src/kernel/clock.ts fire()/#apply/#drain/#due; src/kernel/clock.test.ts "runs every timer when one throws, and still arms at the end of the alarm", "keeps the other deadlines when one timer's due throws" and "tells a caller when the alarm could not be written" fail at a61b166 and pass after
result: kept; a storage write failure still aborts the DO, now after the caller learns about it

decision: A claimed intake batch whose dispatch throws keeps its claim and rejoins the boot replay, a minute out, with the same batch id
why: it was stranded until a reboot with no error and no retry; releasing the claim would have let a retry submit under a new batch id, so a message could land twice, while the replay reuses requestId batch:<batchId> that pi dedupes
evidence: plugins/intake/gateway.ts fire()/dispatch()/fireDue(); plugins/intake/gateway.test.ts "retries a claimed batch whose dispatch throws, and reports the failure" fails at a61b166 (fire rejects and nothing is scheduled) and passes after
result: kept; the failure is logged through ctx.logger, and due() returns the retry time so the alarm wakes for it

decision: The checkpoint proof also asserts that the commit which raced the checkpoint kept its journal row
why: on the merged tree the state assertions alone still held with commit()'s checkpoint gate removed, because the sequence is captured after the snapshot, so the proof did not fail when that behaviour was removed
evidence: removing `while (this.#checkpointing !== undefined) await this.#gate` from src/kernel/journal.ts fails "keeps a commit that lands during a checkpoint out of its snapshot" with "the checkpoint truncated a commit that landed during it: expected 0 to be 1"; the a61b166 journal.ts fails three tests in that file

decision: images() spends its 1 MiB turn budget against the stored size before reading, and only reads an image that still fits
why: the budget was applied after every image had been read in full, so a 50 MB upload was loaded and base64-encoded inside a 128 MB isolate before being discarded
evidence: plugins/intake/attachments.ts images(); plugins/intake/attachments.test.ts "never reads an image that cannot fit the turn budget" fails at 5695ba8 with both paths in port.reads
result: accepted; a file too large to fit is still named in the attachment list

decision: file.delete removes the file row, its revisions and every blob no other row references; drop() also removes the path's revisions
why: only the files row was dropped, so file.revision(s) still served the deleted text and referenced() kept the blob alive, which the sweep could never reclaim
evidence: src/r2env.ts FileIndex.drop/dropUnder; plugins/files/files.ts files.remove; plugins/files/files.test.ts "deletes a file, its revisions and its bytes" fails at 5695ba8 on the surviving revision and both R2 heads
result: accepted; a blob another path still points at is kept, and a failed R2 delete is reclaimed by the weekly sweep

decision: thread.stop commits working or waiting to cancelled itself; a waiting thread no longer holds a threadLimit slot, and its question stops being listed
why: the transition table had no exit from waiting except answer, stop only aborted a conversation that had no run, and liveCount counted waiting against the limit, so eight abandoned questions blocked a project
evidence: src/contracts/threaddoc.ts TRANSITIONS; plugins/orchestrator/threads.ts stopThread/createThread; plugins/orchestrator/service.ts liveCount; plugins/questions/questions.ts openRequests/pendingRequests; plugins/questions/questions.test.ts "stops a waiting thread..." and "does not count a waiting thread..." fail at 5695ba8
result: accepted; the Reporter still writes the status a finished run implies and skips a thread that is no longer working

decision: space.threadIds keeps at most 100 ids per space and drops the oldest finished ones when a new thread takes it past that
why: nothing ever removed an id, so create, list, boot, the watchdog and the question list walked every thread a space ever ran, and the whole workspace document was rewritten each time
evidence: plugins/orchestrator/threads.ts MAX_SPACE_THREADS/trimThreadIds; plugins/orchestrator/orchestrator.test.ts "keeps a space's thread list bounded..." fails at 5695ba8
result: accepted; a pruned thread keeps its document and conversation and can still act in its own scope, but it is no longer listed or reachable through its coordinator

decision: xin.jobs.calls keeps the newest 128 task ids, xin.requests.answered the newest 20 answers, and finished schedules the newest 20
why: each map was appended on every call and never trimmed, so a long-lived home re-serialised its whole history on every job call, answer and fire
evidence: plugins/jobs/jobs.ts trimCalls; plugins/questions/questions.ts trimAnswered; plugins/schedules/schedules.ts pruneFinished; plugins/jobs/jobs.test.ts "keeps the replayed-call map bounded", plugins/questions/questions.test.ts "keeps the answered map bounded", plugins/schedules/schedules.test.ts "drops old finished schedules..." all fail at 5695ba8
result: accepted; the dedupe windows are far wider than a replay needs, and a paused schedule still has a next occurrence so it is never pruned

decision: Done intake rows are pruned on every alarm fire, file.list and one directory listing return at most 1000 paths, and the Dreamer scans only the live task statuses
why: done rows were pruned at boot only, so a long-lived isolate kept every body it dispatched; a listing had no LIMIT; ensurePass paged through every Dreamer task ever created and filtered terminal ones in JS inside a commit
evidence: plugins/intake/gateway.ts expireDone/start/fire; src/r2env.ts MAX_LISTED_FILES/under(); plugins/memory/dreamer.ts liveDreamers; plugins/intake/gateway.test.ts "drops done rows past the retention window...", plugins/files/files.test.ts "bounds one listing to a page of paths" fail at 5695ba8
result: accepted; the Dreamer bound is a scan filter with no public observable, so it is covered by the existing Dreamer tests rather than a new one

decision: The plugins table is dropped by host migration 13 and removed from TABLE_OWNERS; market migration 1 is now empty and version 2 creates market_indexes; market_history, usage_daily, file_revisions and conversation_presets are owned
why: nothing read the plugins table, market created two tables only to drop them, and four plugin-written tables were unknown to the boundary check
evidence: src/db.ts migration 13; src/kernel/dbtables.ts; plugins/market/market.ts MIGRATIONS; src/kernel/db.test.ts "assigns every table a plugin writes...", src/host.test.ts "leaves no table without a reader..." fail at 5695ba8
result: accepted; removing the plugins table needs migration 13 because an existing home still has it, and the market list keeps a version-1 step because the runner requires contiguous versions and a home at 2 must not see the schema move backwards

decision: PatchArg, FileEntry.project and JobRun.models/now/env are gone, and the journal comment names CHECKPOINT_ROWS
why: all were exported or written and never read, leftovers of the storage rewrite
evidence: src/kernel/patch.ts, src/contracts/files.ts, src/contracts/jobs.ts, plugins/jobs/jobs.ts, src/kernel/journal.ts
result: accepted; FileRow.project and the files.project column stay because the index still writes them, and stripTags plus the inbound create/drop steps were left alone as not in the finding list

decision: A schedule run's outcome is read above its own delivered message, so a later owner message no longer hides the reply
why: outcomeOf broke at the first user entry scanning newest-first, and any later owner message is such an entry, so the run stayed running forever
evidence: plugins/schedules/schedules.ts outcomeOf(); plugins/schedules/schedules.test.ts "keeps a run's outcome after a later owner message" fails at 5695ba8 with running
result: accepted; an assistant entry above the run's own message still counts, because pi may answer several messages in one turn

decision: FREQ=HOURLY steps in wall-clock hours, and periodIndex measures local hours, so a DST change does not drift the series
why: hourly slots were fixed milliseconds from the anchor hour, so an every-2-hours rule anchored at local 00:00 gave 03:00, 05:00, 07:00 after spring-forward while the tool promised local clock time
evidence: plugins/schedules/rrule.ts hourlySlots/addMinutes/wallClock/periodIndex/slotStream; plugins/schedules/rrule.test.ts "keeps an hourly wall time across a spring-forward change" fails at 5695ba8; the Lord Howe expectation moves from 16:30Z (03:30 local) to 16:00Z (03:00 local)
result: accepted; the 02:00 slot of a spring-forward day lands at 03:00, and the repeated hour of a fall-back is delivered once

decision: push.flush sends the due held notifications before it rewrites the held list, and keeps one whose send pass throws for five minutes
why: the list was rewritten without the due items first, so a throw in the send pass lost them silently
evidence: plugins/push/push.ts flush(); plugins/push/push.test.ts "keeps a held notification whose send pass throws, for a later retry" fails at 5695ba8 with nothing held
result: accepted; a connected client still drops its due items instead of receiving them late

decision: The web SSRF guard removes a trailing dot from the hostname before judging it
why: localhost. is the same host to DNS but not to a string comparison, so http://localhost./ passed the guard
evidence: plugins/web/web.ts isPrivateHost(); plugins/web/web.test.ts adds http://localhost./ and http://foo.localhost./
result: accepted; 127.0.0.1. was already normalised by the URL parser, localhost. was not

decision: The Worker passes a non-401 answer from the rotated-token check through to the client
why: authorizedByRotation mapped the home's 503 boot_failed to "not ok", so a rotated-token device was told unauthorized while the home was down
evidence: src/worker.ts rotationCheck()/fetch(); src/worker.test.ts "surfaces a boot failure to a rotated-token client instead of a 401" fails at 5695ba8 with 401
result: accepted; a token the home rejects is still a 401, and an unreachable home still answers 401

decision: No change for the intake fire replay finding: the map-based loop from 07fc188 already catches per batch and continues
why: the audit at a61b166 saw the old replay.splice(0) loop, which emptied the queue before resuming; the serious-fix branch replaced it with a map that deletes only the batch it resumed and re-sets a failing one a minute out
evidence: plugins/intake/gateway.ts fire() at 5695ba8; git show 07fc188 -- plugins/intake/gateway.ts
result: reported as already fixed rather than changed again

decision: A submitted job carries its own XIN_LOAD/XIN_LIVE values, the runner hands them to the child, and two jobs with different variants do not coalesce
why: the cache key is computed by the run child, so with the runner's environment deciding both, a XIN_LOAD=1 submission answered by a runner started without it ran the normal suite and reported a pass
evidence: while a runner started without XIN_LOAD was alive, `XIN_LOAD=1 bun scripts/gate.ts submit test --only=plugins/web` reported test:pass with the web tests in .gate/test.log; after the change the same submission runs under XIN_LOAD=1, where vitest finds no bench file under plugins/web, and `XIN_LOAD=1 bun scripts/gate.ts submit test` runs test/load.bench.ts
result: kept; the runner itself is spawned without either variable, and each variant keeps its own cache slot and log, so alternating the suite and the benchmark does not evict either

decision: The schedule-outcome proof now appends the later owner message as a pi.user entry
why: the logged proof was not a proof: the later message submitted through root.submit was still queued when the test read the entries, so the run's reply was never hidden and the test passed at 5695ba8 as well
evidence: with the old body the test passed on the 5695ba8 worktree (plugins/schedules/schedules.test.ts, 20 tests, 1 failed: only the prune test); with the new body it fails at 5695ba8 with [ 'running' ] and passes at HEAD
result: kept; the entry is written the way the gateway's input submission writes it, tx.appendEntry(UserEntry, ...)

decision: A home at version 12 is proved to open and lose the plugins table; host_migrations is one singleton row, not one row per version
why: src/host.test.ts proved only a fresh boot, and an existing home is the only reason step 13 exists; deleting the version row instead of setting it back made the runner replay step 1 and fail the boot with 503
evidence: src/host.test.ts "drops the plugins table from a home that was created before migration 13": UPDATE host_migrations SET version = 12, system.restart, table gone, version 13, GET /v1/status 200; removing step 13 from src/db.ts fails it

decision: A Worker can clone and read git itself with a hand-written pack reader: one smart-HTTP v2 fetch, a git v2 .idx built with workerd's native zlib, pack + idx in R2 (3 writes)
why: the question was whether git runs on the Worker at all; isomorphic-git runs but costs 27.5 s for a 10 MB repo in the Worker, while the same clone with node:zlib and a 400-line reader is 3.5 s
evidence: test/git-native/ on branch git/native-worker; express full (9.7 MB, 32,576 objects) 3,532 ms in wrangler dev, log 1 ms, diff 3 ms; isomorphic-git 27,465 ms; docs/reports/2026-11-10-native-git-in-worker.md
result: prototype only, not shipped: 16-git.md still says no clone; a real row needs incremental fetch, R2 range reads and a pack-size policy

decision: The object store is one pack object plus one index object in R2, not one R2 object per git object
why: a per-object store costs a Class A write per object at clone time and buys nothing, because reading a pack is already lazy and inflates only the objects a request touches
evidence: chalk 1,706 objects: pack mode 37 ms of writes, loose mode 6,798 ms and 1,709 writes; docs/reports/2026-11-10-native-git-in-worker.md
result: pack mode kept in the prototype; loose mode exists only as the comparison

decision: The pack reader never passes maxOutputLength to node:zlib inflateSync
why: workerd throws RangeError: Memory limit exceeded for some maxOutputLength values (65,536 and 98,304 fail, 32,768 and 130,048 succeed) even when the output is a few hundred bytes; the same call without the hint works
evidence: GET /zlib?kb=64 on wrangler dev fails, /zlib?kb=64&nomax=1 succeeds; test/git-native/pack.ts inflate() checks the inflated length against the pack header instead
result: adopted; the length check also catches a corrupt pack

decision: The native git row stores one pack, one v2 .idx and one span table per repository in R2, reads objects by R2 range, and keeps refs, the head and the shallow boundary in SQLite
why: a cold read must not pull a 4.5 MB pack to answer a 5-commit log, and a read must not re-derive refs from the pack; the index is tens of KB and each object a few hundred bytes
evidence: gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner depth 5 (2,420 objects, 4.5 MB pack): first read 13 ms / 14 range reads / 92 KB, second read in the same isolate 4 ms / 12 reads / 5 KB, third read with the same reader 0 ms / 0 reads; plugins/git-native
result: kept; the 2 MB whole-pack path keeps small repositories at one read

decision: The pack ceiling is 80 MB and a repository past it is re-fetched with filter blob:none, which keeps commits and trees and drops file contents
why: a 330 MB pack crashed the workerd runtime in the prototype, and the ceiling must degrade rather than kill the isolate; the download is streamed and cancelled at the cap so the oversized pack is never held
evidence: vercel/next.js full history crashed workerd at ~330 MB; the fixture test 'keeps history only when the full pack passes the ceiling' clones with maxBytes 1200, lands on partial=1, answers diff with patch null and show through one extra want
result: accepted; a repository too large even for a history-only clone is refused with a message

decision: A refresh asks for the refs only and re-clones the pack when the head moved; there is no have/negotiation yet
why: an unchanged head should cost nothing, and a real incremental fetch is the expensive part of the protocol; the cheap half is worth having now
evidence: same repository cloned twice: reused true, 2 requests, 94 KB, 1.4 s, 0 R2 reads and 0 writes; a moved head pays a full clone

decision: The journal is a ring of SLOTS = CHECKPOINT_ROWS + 32 slots (pi_journal_ring, PK (slot, part), WITHOUT ROWID) overwritten by upsert; a checkpoint upserts its row and parts and deletes nothing; a full ring holds the flush in memory and retries the checkpoint; a pre-ring pi_journal is replayed, checkpointed and dropped at open
why: a DELETE bills one row written per row, so truncating 256 rows per checkpoint doubled the journal's write cost; an overwriting upsert bills one row like an insert; the legacy table is migrated by checkpoint rather than copied into slots because a home whose checkpoints failed can hold more uncovered rows than the ring has slots; the 32 spare slots, not 256, keep a cold boot's full ring scan small, and PRAGMA table_list replaces a sqlite_master scan that read 16-40 rows a boot
evidence: INGLE_LOAD=1 test/load: turnPerMessage writes 16 -> 12, reads 21 -> 17; harnessPerTurn writes 9 -> 8, reads 11 -> 9; turn-window SQL writes 4089 -> 2022; whole-run SQL writes 4757 -> 2431; DELETE pi_journal 2304w gone; coldBoot reads 281 -> 315 (288 slots + 27); coldJournalRows 254 unchanged; src/cost.test.ts message 13w/15r unchanged; journal.test.ts wrap-around with a stale multi-part slot, restore after a checkpoint with 44 uncovered slots, and full-ring hold all pass
result: accepted; spec 11 §18 updated; load bounds lowered (writes/message 22 -> 16, reads/message 32 -> 23, harness 40/24 -> 12/11)

evidence: plugins/drive/drive.test.ts: versions survive write/checkout/move, AGENTS.md served from cache after its blob is deleted and reloaded after a write, a cached turn reads no more rows than a home without Drive files, legacy kv skill moved on evict, thread grant opens /captains/<own>/ only

decision: The Home DO is the auth boundary: Home.fetch checks the deploy token or the rotated digest held in memory (read once from kv via raw storage, replaced by session.rotate) on every route; the Worker rejects bearer-less requests and pre-checks only PUT /files

decision: POST /v1/cmd accepts an array of up to 32 frames run in order; the web client batches commands issued in one task and caches pure reads by op+args, cleared by any successful command and by a home snap

decision: The compact row installs a beforeCompact hook: a threshold compaction whose replaced messages hold a tool result over 2,000 chars and fit 5,000 tokens once each such result is cut to head+tail is placed as that pruned transcript with no model call; anything else is summarized on the owner's utility model, else left to pi
why: pi 1.5 lets a hook only decline or supply a summary, not edit entries, so pruning is a deterministic summary; the budget is a quarter of keepRecentTokens so the post-compaction context stays well under the background threshold; the utility model moves the summary off the chat model; manual and overflow compactions are never prune-only
evidence: plugins/compact/compact.test.ts on the 5x43 KB tool-result transcript: summary requests 1 (12,069 bytes, on the chat model) before, 0 after, placed summary 10,680 chars with head and tail and no middle; prune-insufficient transcript: 1 request of 60,070 bytes on the chat model before, 1 of 60,019 bytes on the utility model after; no utility default still uses pi's request

decision: The compact hook adds each utility summary response's usage to the conversation's pi.usage in its own harness commit, mirroring pi's recordUsage

evidence: plugins/compact/compact.test.ts: the root's pi.usage holds faux-dream/dream-1 with totalTokens > 0 after a utility summary, and the assertion fails with the charge removed

decision: The utility usage charge is an immediate harness commit, not persistence: deferred
why: a deferred commit is stored by the next commit that touches pi.usage or after settings.progress.persistWithinMs (about 1 s); the next pi.usage commit is the next model response, usually later than that, so deferring would rarely fold the row and would risk losing the charge on a crash
evidence: pi-durable session.js #deferral returns undefined without persistence.kind "deferred"; plugins/compact/summary.ts chargeUsage passes no options; spec 13-always-on states one immediate journal row per utility response, two commits on the utility path like pi's own

decision: Manifest v3 keeps api 1 and accepts that a third-party code package injecting a guarded service without declaring its permission stops mounting
why: api is the hard compatibility axis, but no third-party code package is in package.json today and bumping it would make every shipped manifest restate api 2 for no reader; the failure names the missing permission, so the fix for an author is one line
evidence: review of xin#19 (XIN-23, low); package.json dependencies hold no ingle code package

decision: client, slots and the client module specifier leave the manifest until the PR that adds the web slot loader
why: nothing in xin#19 read them (CREW rule: no speculative code)
evidence: review of xin#19 (XIN-23, low)

decision: Install consent in the market: install, update and rollback compute the permissions a version needs (code from its declared ingle.plugins permissions, bundles from the compiled plugins their verified rows mount, git as runtime) and reject with consent_required and { permissions: [{ id, title, why }] } when grant and the held permissions leave one out; a consent rejection writes no receipt
why: the AMA-17 brief asks for install-time consent; held permissions come from the package's mounted rows so an update asks only for what is new; git code cannot be read before the build, so it asks for the strongest permission; a receipt would answer the granted retry with the stale rejection when the client reuses the command id
evidence: plugins/market/market.test.ts: a secrets-mounting bundle is refused, stores nothing, is refused again under the same command id, installs with grant, and updates with no new prompt; a code update adding network and secrets asks for both, then for secrets alone after granting network

decision: A pending code install carries the registry's dist.integrity, served by /v1/build/packages, and plugin sync refuses a lockfile that resolves the spec to another SRI
why: consent covers the package.json the market read; without a pin the build could install other bytes under the same version range or a republished tag; bun.lock already records the SRI, so the check is a lockfile read with no network
evidence: test/lockfile.test.ts accepts the consented SRI and refuses another or a non-registry resolution; market.test.ts shows the SRI in the pending list

decision: Permission checks are scoped honestly: for shipped and built-in rows they hold against accidental reach on every service lookup path (internal/get hook, a reflect.get wrapper, a re-attributed ctx.root, caller checks in secrets/ops/wire, module-private service state), with Cordis escape hatches and computed imports refused at build for local and npm packages; a market code install runs with owner trust and its permissions describe what it declares, not a sandbox
why: plugins share one isolate, so in-isolate checks cannot make untrusted code safe (Bosun, 2026-11-16); private fields cannot hide state behind Cordis's method proxies
evidence: review of xin#19 at 2c40e40 (XIN-23: ctx.root, reflect.get, private fields, lint gaps); k-reach negative control: 13 of 14 routes reached with the guards stubbed

decision: A code install's consent and pin come from its verified tarball: the market fetches it within the bundle caps, checks the sha512 dist.integrity, reads permissions from package/package.json, and records { integrity, tarball, permissions } as the pending spec's pin; plugin sync verifies the tarball bytes before bun add and refuses a bun.lock SRI or an installed package.json permission outside the pin
why: npm does not tie the version document to the tarball (manifest confusion), so permissions read from metadata could differ from what builds
evidence: review of xin#35 at 6c940ee (XIN-23); test 'reads a code package's permissions from its verified tarball' fails on the old market

decision: A market bundle's patch asks consent for each row it enables or reconfigures, is refused on a kernel row, and its requires must already be in the build
why: patch and requires were outside bundleNeeds, so a bundle could switch on tool-web or tool-plugins or record unconsented code
evidence: review of xin#35 (XIN-23, Devin); patch test fails on the old market

decision: Add from URL calls market.add, which takes an exact name@x.y.z through the market's consent and pin (a git spec asks for runtime); plugin.install stays as the unchecked kernel op for the owner's own CLI and API
why: the owner path must not skip consent, but the kernel op is how a pipeline or the owner scripts installs, and only the owner can call it
evidence: review of xin#35 (XIN-23); add test fails on the old market

decision: A compiled package the market installed (it has a market_history row) is installed at its compiled version, not provided: its index entry wins over the build's, and its held permissions are its compiled plugins' manifests
why: before, held read only runtime bundles and a built code package was 'provided', so every update asked again and none could apply
evidence: review of xin#35 (XIN-23); held test with an installed v1 fails on the old market

decision: Issues live in plugin-owned SQLite tables (issues, issue_states, issue_assignees, issue_links, issue_events, issues_fts) with JSON list columns on the issue row, not in a pi document
why: a list must be one query and FTS search needs SQLite; a doc would reload every issue on each change. Denormalized labels/assignees/threads/prs keep the list a single SELECT, and issue_assignees indexes the assignee filter
evidence: plugins/issues/cost.test.ts: create 9 rows written, comment 7, a 20-issue list 21 rows read, get 7

decision: Issue wakes go through intake as job items (owner thread on comment/state/assignee change, newly assigned threads, mentioned conversations), never the actor itself
why: intake already debounces and batches; no new inbound kind is needed and the intake contract stays unchanged
evidence: plugins/issues/issues.test.ts wake tests

decision: The agent tool is one compact issue tool with an action field, and its row tool-issues ships disabled
why: four tools added about 3.2 KB to every request and broke the turn and first-thread byte bounds in src/cost.test.ts; one tool roughly halves that, and shipping it off keeps the shared bounds unchanged, like web and git
evidence: src/cost.test.ts failed at 87741>78000 promptBytes with four tools on; passes with the row off

decision: Issue wakes go through an outbox table (issue_wakes) written in the mutation's transaction, delivered after commit and replayed at boot
why: a crash between the issue commit and the intake enqueue lost the wake; intake commandIds keep replay idempotent
evidence: plugins/issues/review.test.ts outbox replay test

decision: Agent comments stop waking after 3 agent comments in a row since a person last acted

decision: The picker reads models.catalog (owner-only, capped at 200 models) instead of models.list; enabled-ness is stored as an owner.disabled list; thinking widens to pi-ai MODEL_THINKING_LEVELS and conv.configure rejects a level the model does not support
why: the UI needs providers, prices, reasoning levels, favourites and per-key enablement in one read; a disabled list keeps every keyed model enabled by default with no write; pi-ai 1.5 has no fast or service-tier mode, so no modes field is invented
evidence: plugins/models/models.test.ts catalog test; gate lint types test green

decision: Disabling a model moves every conversation on it (home chat, coordinators and Captains, threads) to the default its role resolves to (project, then owner), applied by models.enable itself; with no default left the model is cleared so the next turn asks for one; a model that is an owner or project role default cannot be disabled; every path that picks a model (conv.configure, set_model, models.list, owner.defaults, project.update, captain.create/update, delegate_task incl. its parent fallback, thread.create, thread.side) refuses a disabled one through ModelsService.disabled
why: Bosun decision: conversations on a disabled model switch to their role default at their next turn and new threads never inherit it; moving them eagerly at the toggle costs one commit per affected conversation once, instead of a check on every request
evidence: plugins/models/models.test.ts disabled-paths and move tests

decision: Spend is attributed per feature at flush time from each conversation's pi.usage growth (usage_feature table, usage.marks in kv); background calls are charged into pi.usage under a <feature>: key prefix; per-feature caps are checked where work starts (message.send, delegate_task, goal rounds, Dreamer, compaction) rather than in a GenerationTask hook
why: pi records usage per conversation and model only, so the feature has to come from the conversation or from a tagged key; a throwing beforeRequest hook is reported and skipped by pi (README: a throwing hook is reported and skipped), so a hook cannot stop a request; checking at admission costs 0 extra rows because caps and the month's per-feature totals are held in memory
evidence: plugins/models/budget.test.ts: feature booking, cap refusal on message.send, 2 usage_feature rows written for 2 changed (feature, model) pairs and 0 on an idle flush; full gate 577 tests

decision: Features sum to usage_daily: the flush walks every conversation through a new ctx.pi.conversations() (MemoryStorage scan) and books unclaimed spend as a new `other` feature, tools included; compaction summaries are made by the hook on the utility model then the conversation's model and charged `compaction`; caps also gate thread.create, thread.side, thread.send, report delivery (skipped when the coordinator's feature is capped) and automation runs (failed with the cap reason; after #23 replaced schedules); feature passes are serialized; a goal on a chat books as `goal`; admit adds unflushed in-memory spend and reuses its classifications at the next flush
why: Bosun on #38: features must sum to the total and every start point must be gated; pi has no conversation listing on Harness, but the harness runs on MemoryStorage so a scan is free, which avoids a residual that could go negative; skipping a capped report or occurrence keeps the cap hard while leaving the result on the thread doc and the schedule's next occurrence intact
evidence: plugins/models/budget.test.ts sum (root, Puck chat, coordinator, thread, tool, unlisted), root goal, unflushed delegate refusal with 0 writes, thread.create/side cap 0; compact.test.ts three summary paths; automations.test.ts automation cap and tracking; budget.test.ts overlapping flushes book once; settled.test.ts capped report; dreamer.test.ts real pass

decision: A resume answer applies only to the subscribers its cursor came from; every subscribe sends a plain sub; an "unknown frame" error during a resume makes the client resend plain subs
why: XIN-23: a subscriber that joined mid-reconnect applied a delta to an empty window, and a rolled-back server froze views by refusing resume
evidence: web/src/lib/api.test.ts "Streams on a reconnect": late joiner gets only the snap, second subscriber sends a sub, refused resume falls back; all fail before the fix

decision: The automations row imports the session-scoped xin.schedules document at boot: each record becomes automation sched-<id> (DAILY/WEEKLY/HOURLY with INTERVAL=1 and BYDAY/BYHOUR/BYMINUTE becomes a 5-field cron in the record tz, missing BYHOUR/BYMINUTE/BYDAY taken from the anchor as the old rule did; a future at becomes a once trigger; COUNT, UNTIL, INTERVAL>1, MONTHLY or a future DTSTART import disabled with no trigger and the original RRULE appended to the prompt). this_session and a reserved new_once keep their conversation as a same-thread target, new becomes fresh in the origin conversation's project, active becomes enabled. A slot due and not delivered per the record cursor (an at that never ran, a deploy mid-send, a slot missed while the home slept) is queued once as run legacy:<id>:<slot> before the automation is created, so create's arm fires it at the next wake. Then the document is retired in its own commit
why: review finding (High): the PR dropped every existing schedule on upgrade. Queuing the run with store.addRun instead of engine.trigger avoids dispatching thread.create during plugin apply; the derived automation and run ids make a boot that crashed before the retire repeat the import without duplicates. A failed import is logged and keeps the document for the next boot instead of failing the plugin
evidence: plugins/automations/legacy.test.ts
result: adopted; an unmappable schedule that was mid-send is not re-run because its due slot cannot be computed without the old RRULE engine

decision: automations.revision floors at the wall clock: it starts at Date.now() on boot and each change sets max(revision + 1, Date.now()). Nothing is stored and no migration is added
why: Deviation from 'persist it in the same row write': automation.delete writes no row a counter could ride on, so a stored counter costs one extra row write per change, a delete included. Clients compare the revision only for change, and a value floored at the wall clock never repeats across an eviction. The only exception would be more than one change per millisecond sustained up to the eviction. Bosun accepted this in place of a stored counter: the revision still rises across a reboot, with no migration and no extra row write. In memory over a stored rev because the projection already sees every xin.requests commit and reads every requests doc at boot, so the counter costs no row read or write per open, resolve or snapshot; flooring at Date.now() (the plugins/automations precedent) keeps it from repeating across eviction, and an eviction alone moves it once, which costs one request.list on reconnect

decision: The reduce-motion blocks of ingle-motion.css restate the selectors they reset at matching or higher specificity: .im-swap > :not([data-active]), .im-swap-icon > :not([data-active]), .im-tab[data-closing], .im-lift[data-settling], and the press rules as .im-press:active:not(:disabled, [aria-disabled="true"]) and .im-send:active:not(:disabled); the same text sits in the OS media query and :root[data-motion="reduce"]
why: Under the OS rule the bare resets (.im-swap > *, .im-tab, .im-lift at (0,1,0); .im-press:active, .im-send:active at (0,2,0)) lost to the (0,2,0) and (0,3,0) rules they were meant to undo, so swaps blurred and scaled, closing tabs shrank, a dropped tab slid, and buttons still pressed in; the in-app setting worked only because its :root prefix raises specificity. Fixed at the source, and the drive handoff copy matches byte for byte
evidence: Chromium computed styles with reducedMotion reduce, before -> after: inactive icon swap scale(.6) blur(2px) -> none; text swap translateY(4px) blur(2px) -> none; closing tab scale(.96) over 140 ms -> no transform, opacity only over --dur-reduce (120 ms); settling lift translate/transform/box-shadow 200/140/140 ms -> no transition; .im-press and .im-send while held scale(.97) -> none. With :root[data-motion="reduce"] the closing tab (real classes im-tab im-lift im-flip) used to vanish instantly, because :root[data-motion="reduce"] .im-flip { transition: none } at (0,3,0) beat .im-tab[data-closing]'s durations; it now fades over 120 ms like the OS path. decision: A stored attachment records the files index's path, type, size and sha256 at message.send, and a turn reads its bytes by sha256 (files.readBlob)

decision: One rolldown codeSplitting group, vendor, takes every node_modules module tagged $initial (statically reached from the entry); startup JS drops from 264,996 to 252,233 bytes gzip -9 (main a07d81f7) and from 37 to 14 chunks; the startup set gains two @ui-sdk/core list modules (async-options, listbox-value, about 10.8 KB source) that the entry reaches through the lists barrel and main shipped only lazily

decision: web tests own their globals and module state: web/test/globals.ts stubGlobals installs each file's own stubs in beforeAll and restores the exact descriptors in afterAll, deleting any that were absent; files whose modules read window at import (tabs, onboarding, plugin-detail, skill-detail, integration-row) import them in beforeAll; api, cmd and socket tests restore descriptors after each test instead of reassigning values; onboarding resets with loadProgress before each test; context.test gives each test its own conversation ids

Reassigning a saved undefined left an own property behind
evidence: XIN-23 review of #98 at 5b9f4117. Filtered repro (tabs, plugin-detail, context, onboarding with -t) crashed on window.location.hash at 5b9f4117 and passes now, plain and with --seed=98765; a preload that compares global descriptors before and after each file found six leaking files at 5b9f4117 and none now; bun test src --randomize with seeds 1, 2, 3, 7, 42, 98765, 31337, 2026, 555, 8080: 330/330 each
